newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. demands freedom of movement in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. demands freedom of movement in Bosnia.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher warned Bosnia's factions on Thursday that the United Nations would consider sanctions against them unless they allowed freedom of movement in their ethnically-divided state.

His warning, at an international conference aimed at speeding implementation of the Dayton peace accords, followed clashes this week between Bosnian Serbs and Moslems trying to return to former homes in what is now Serb territory.

Christopher said: "We will hold the parties to an increasingly greater level of responsibility for the functions such as assuring freedom of movement and resettlement of refugees now undertaken or coordinated by the international community."
He warned: "We have made it clear to the parties that the Security Council will consider imposing measures if they fail to significantly meet their obligations under the peace agreement.
"We will link economic reconstruction assistance to the implementastion by the parties of the Agreement - including cooperation with the War Crimes Tribunal."
